ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A creeping plant twists exactly 5 times around a post with circumference $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ (as shown in the diagram) and thus reaches a height of $1 \mathrm{~m}$. While the plant grows the height of the plant also grows with constant speed. How long is the creeping plant?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a vertical cylindrical pole can be seen, and a vine/climbing plant grows upward by spirally winding around the pole. On the right side of the pole there is a vertical height scale, labeled as 1 m. Reasoning: The problem gives that the plant winds exactly 5 turns around the pole, the circumference of the pole is 15 cm, and the total vertical height is 1 m = 100 cm. After unfolding the cylindrical side surface into a plane rectangle, each turn corresponds to traveling one circumference, 15 cm, in the horizontal direction, so the horizontal distance of 5 turns is 5 × 15 = 75 cm. The vertical distance is 100 cm. Since the height increases uniformly with growth, after unfolding, the vine corresponds to a straight diagonal line in the rectangle; therefore the length of the vine is sqrt(75^2 + 100^2) = sqrt(5625 + 10000) = sqrt(15625) = 125 cm = 1.25 m.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a vine spiraling around a vertical cylindrical post, with a vertical height marker labeled 1 m alongside the post. Use the text for the exact data: the vine makes 5 complete twists around a post whose circumference is 15 cm, and the total vertical rise is 1 m. Unroll the cylindrical surface of the post into a rectangle: each full twist contributes one horizontal circumference of 15 cm, so 5 twists give horizontal distance 5 × 15 = 75 cm. The vertical distance is 1 m = 100 cm. The vine becomes the diagonal of this unrolled rectangle, so its length is sqrt(75^2 + 100^2) = sqrt(15625) = 125 cm = 1.25 m.
